design_notes.consequence: Classes whose tolerance cannot be met at any ratio are BLOCKED; capital efficiency of long terms collapses before the risk does.
design_notes.fix: Rule change (out of scope for tuning): a claim/top-up path during the term (e.g. RED-4 from lockHeight at a higher threshold), term-scaled ratios, or shorter maximum terms.
design_notes.text: The vault script admits only the owner path until claimHeight, so the base ratio must cover the whole term's drawdown. P(bad debt) at the shipped ratios: A 0.45%, B 2.74%, C 20.44% (tolerances 0.50%, 1.00%, 2.00%); the lowest reachable within the registry bounds: A 0.32%, B 2.74%, C 20.44%. At the upper bound each class meets its tolerance only for terms up to A 71 d, B 0 d, C 0 d (class maxima 90, 365, 1825 d), and a vault that is bad at the claim opening is short by 19%, 41%, 57% of its debt on average. A bad vault is not yet a realised loss: nobody may claim it below the debt, it stays claimable if the price recovers, and YED holders bear the gap only through the peg (D-RD-AUD-3).
design_notes.title: No liquidation before lockHeight + grace (fact 1.5-1)

design_notes.consequence: residualMinZat only matters under RED-4(b); raising claimThresholdBps transfers more value from absent owners to claimants.
design_notes.fix: Rule change: cap the RED-4(a) claimant at debt × (1 + a bounty) and return the rest.
design_notes.text: The claimant cap uses the same threshold that made the vault underwater, so a RED-4(a) claimant takes the whole collateral; an absent owner forfeits everything above the debt (mean forfeit at the first trigger: 511 bps of the debt).
design_notes.title: RED-5 residual is always 0 under RED-4(a)

design_notes.consequence: Claimants do not show up in a steady decline; abandoned vaults drift into bad debt.
design_notes.fix: Parameter (claimThresholdBps, see its recommendation) or a rule change: a fresher claim price (e.g. pFast or the attested aClaim for RED-4(a)).
design_notes.text: pClaim = max(pMid, pSlow) lags a falling price, so when a vault first shows underwater the claimant's expected margin is 236 bps of the debt at the current threshold (show-up rate 63%; already bad debt at the trigger: 22%).
design_notes.title: pClaim lag eats the claim margin

design_notes.consequence: The emergency path's benefit depends on a YED discount appearing in a crash.
design_notes.fix: Rule change: pay the RED-4(b) claimant at pEmerg (or with a bounty).
design_notes.text: Under RED-4(b) the claimant receives the debt's worth at pClaim, the higher of the two prices, so at par it is a loss (2197 bps of the debt on average in the crash runs); it only works as a par exit for YED holders when YED trades at a discount.
design_notes.title: RED-4(b) never pays a claimant buying YED at par

design_notes.consequence: Ratios are sized at multiplier 1×; G2 (sigmaRefBps) decides whether that changes.
design_notes.fix: Parameter coupling with G2, not a rule change.
design_notes.text: The median hour-mode σ multiplier over the ensemble is 10000 bps (σ̂ on the smoothed pFast stays below sigmaRefBps, D-WP3-6), so the base ratio alone carries the drawdown budget.
design_notes.title: The σ multiplier adds no protection at its median

design_notes.consequence: Boundary moves only shift the problem between classes.
design_notes.fix: Rule change: more classes, or a ratio that grows with the lock length.
design_notes.text: P(bad debt) rises with the term inside each class (heterogeneity A 3.34, B 1.59, C 1.08 against 0.5); with three fixed classes (NUM_CLASSES) and one ratio per class, long terms are under-collateralised relative to short ones.
design_notes.title: Term heterogeneity inside the classes

design_notes.consequence: A longer abandonBlocks protects slow developers but keeps vaults locked longer when they are truly gone; the parameter cannot serve both.
design_notes.fix: Policy (set dev_absence_tolerance_days) or a rule change (an explicit developer liveness signal).
design_notes.text: With abandonBlocks 34560 (30 d), developers who return after more than 12 days cannot ship a freeze-then-fix set (M14 lead 16128 + buffer 4608) before owners may sweep: abandonment and a slow fix race.
design_notes.title: Abandonment tolerates only a short developer absence

design_notes.consequence: Owner continuity is bought with collateral (G3 must size ratios for lock + grace).
design_notes.fix: Rule change: allow RED-4 claims from lockHeight at a lower threshold while the owner path stays open.
design_notes.text: The grace window adds 0.33% (A), 0.55% (B), 0.80% (C) to P(bad debt) at the shipped values because nobody can claim during it (fact 1.5-1); for class A a 30-day grace is 33–100 % of the term.
design_notes.title: Grace is drawdown exposure for short terms

design_notes.text: G7 design note (cap-exempt liquidation): the worst-day liquidation demand of class-A vaults alone ($4,278, p95 of the worst crash) exceeds max_depth_fraction of the p10 daily YEC volume ($2,500). Class A at σ = 1 sits exactly at recapRatioBps and bypasses MINT-6 (W20), so supplyCapBps cannot bound it; only a rule change (cap-exempt supply counted against its own limit) or a higher class-A ratio would. The depth figure is a placeholder unless a depth file is loaded.

G6 design note (FEE-1 base): FEE-1 is a share of the vault's collateral, so a vault's round-trip fee as a share of its debt is 2·feeBps·baseRatio at every size — 1.78% for class A (ARMED) at the current values, above max_fee_share_small for any feeBps > 11 bps. Levying FEE-1 on the debt value (mintedCents at pMint) would make the fee class-neutral; that is a rule change, out of scope for tuning.

an entity with 25% of the seated weight holds 34.8% of a bundle's weight when selected, so it spans qLow in 0% of bundles at the current value (proposal §7.2 states the rule for the *selected* attestors). Griefing only (aMint down → over-collateralisation); theft (aMint up) needs > 65%: P = 0.000.

design_notes.consequence: minMint (cents) and feeMin (zat) drift apart as the YEC price moves; a USD-stable floor needs a new parameter set after large price moves.
design_notes.fix: Rule change (feeMin in cents at pMint) or periodic re-sets.
design_notes.text: Above $1.20/YEC the 0.5-YEC floor, not feeBps, sets a minMint vault's fee; at the policy's worst price the round-trip share of a minMint debt is 100% (class C).
design_notes.title: feeMin is denominated in YEC
